sources.title: On geometric inverse problems and microlocal analysis
sources.work_type: Expository lecture notes based on 2021 minicourses; arXiv record reports 60 pages.
sources.extraction_coverage: 60/60 PDF pages; text extraction includes explicit page markers 1 through 60.
sources.read_coverage: Complete pp. 1-60, in bounded consecutive page blocks; includes the full Radon/geodesic X-ray, wave Gelfand, Calderón, nonlinear equation, exercises, and references sections.
important_locators: §2.1, pp. 4-7: Fourier slice theorem, Euclidean Radon injectivity, exact normal operator and filtered backprojection; Exercise 2.1 poses an L2 Sobolev stability estimate.
§§2.2-2.4, pp. 7-19: simple-manifold hypotheses, elliptic normal operator, counterexamples/open questions, Pestov identity proof route.
§3, pp. 20-39: hyperbolic DN map, integral identity, light-ray recovery, geometric optics/Gaussian beams, finite-time visibility limit.
§4, pp. 39-57: conductivity and Schrödinger DN maps, boundary determination, transversally anisotropic uniqueness, CGO/Carleman route, nonlinear cubic recovery.
pp. 58-60: reference metadata and frontier context.
limitations: No general quantitative stability modulus is proved for the PDE coefficient inverse problems in this text.
The geodesic X-ray injectivity proof is explicitly simplified to 2D and compactly supported interior functions; broader theorem points to PSU23 for details.
General-manifold Calderón uniqueness, partial-data uniqueness in the stated linear setting, and several time-dependent/Lorentzian questions are stated as open.
The Euclidean Radon stability estimate in Exercise 2.1 is stated as an exercise, not included as a proof.

sources.title: A general support theorem for analytic double fibration transforms
sources.work_type: Research article; arXiv record reports 46 pages.
sources.extraction_coverage: 46/46 PDF pages; text extraction includes explicit page markers 1 through 46.
sources.read_coverage: Complete pp. 1-46, in bounded consecutive page blocks; includes all theorem statements, double-fibration/Bolker geometry, analytic FBI proof, applications, and references.
important_locators: Theorems 1.1-1.8, pp. 1-9: analytic wavefront recovery, local support/uniqueness, analytic 2D geodesic injectivity, null bicharacteristics, and generalized transforms.
§§2-3, pp. 11-19: double fibration Fourier-integral representation and geometric equivalences for Bolker condition.
§4, pp. 19-27: ray-transform flows, conjugate points, geodesic and null-bicharacteristic visibility conditions.
§5, pp. 27-42: full analytic microlocal recovery proof by wave packets/FBI transforms, complex stationary phase and phase positivity.
§6, pp. 42-44: analytic continuation/layer-stripping applications and their hypotheses; pp. 44-46 references.
limitations: Requires analytic structure and a local Bolker condition for analytic wavefront recovery; this is not a general smooth-category uniqueness result.
Local support theorem requires one-sided vanishing across a hypersurface and a visible conormal direction.
Global geodesic uniqueness in the 2D theorem additionally assumes strict convexity, nontrapping and analytic metric, with layer stripping.
The article establishes qualitative uniqueness/support, not quantitative noisy-data stability or a reconstruction algorithm.
When Bolker fails, the text describes artifact-generating branches; no universal injectivity assertion is made for geometries with conjugate points.

supplier_inventory.boundary: Published suppliers are forward PDE/functional-analysis/scattering foundations only. No local carrier was identified for the inverse uniqueness, microlocal visibility, CGO, Gaussian beam, or quantitative PDE inverse stability theorems.

advanced_prerequisite_annex.purpose: Proof-closure contracts for scaffold claims IP-39, IP-40, and IP-41. These are proposed prerequisite obligations, not claims that the reader has authored or locally proved the modules.

proposed_modules.contract: For oriented X,G and embedded Z subset G x X with both projections submersions and dim(G)+dim(X)>dim(Z)>dim(G)>=dim(X), define a smooth nonvanishing weighted fiber integral and prove its conormal canonical relation via local graph coordinates and the delta/conormal kernel.
proposed_modules.source_status: MST §§2.1-2.2, pp. 11-15 proves the specialized kernel and relation; uses general Hörmander conormal/FIO conventions.

proposed_modules.contract: Define Bolker as injective immersion of pi_L; prove global fiber injectivity and differential rank tests separately, with variation/Jacobi criteria for ray transforms and explicit restricted-data hypotheses.
proposed_modules.source_status: MST §§3-4, pp. 16-27 proves equivalences and applications; no-conjugate-points alone is not an unrestricted replacement for the rank hypotheses.

proposed_modules.contract: Define analytic wavefront regularity by a specified Gaussian/FBI transform and prove a sufficient analytic stationary-phase estimate with a unique nondegenerate complex critical point, positive quadratic imaginary phase, and exponential error bound.
proposed_modules.source_status: MST §§5.1-5.6, pp. 27-42 proves its tailored kernel reduction, critical-point and phase estimates; cites Sjöstrand's general FBI characterization and analytic stationary phase. General foundations must be supplied locally or replaced by a fully proved specialized lemma.

proposed_modules.contract: Under analytic double-fibration hypotheses and Bolker at a canonical point, prove WF_a data regularity implies object-covector regularity for compactly supported distributions. Separately state one-sided vanishing across a C2 hypersurface and absence of its conormal analytic singularity as hypotheses for local vanishing.
proposed_modules.source_status: MST Theorems 1.2-1.3 and §§5-6 prove/apply the specialized result; analytic FBI/FIO wavefront calculus and general microlocal continuation are cited foundations, not re-proved from first principles.

IP-40_variable_metric_wave_and_beams.existing_supplier_limit: Published Euclidean constant-speed energy, terminal uniqueness, and finite propagation items do not establish variable Riemannian wave IBVP well-posedness or correction estimates.

proposed_modules.contract: For compact smooth (M,g), smooth boundary, real q, compatible smooth data, and (d_t^2-Delta_g+q)u=F, prove finite-time existence/uniqueness, energy bounds, and a zero-initial-data correction estimate in the beam construction norm; specify coercive shift and terminal-data reversal.
proposed_modules.source_status: Salo §3.3, pp. 30-32 uses a correction estimate and §3.1 derives the identity; well-posedness is referred to Evans, not proved in the notes.

proposed_modules.contract: Under simple geometry or explicit global polar coordinates, construct the phase t-r, solve transport equations, and prove residual/concentration estimates and exact correction with time-delay/length/support hypotheses.
proposed_modules.source_status: Salo §3.3, pp. 26-32 supplies the construction in detail; simplicity-to-global-polar-coordinate fact is referred to PSU23 §§3.7-3.8.

proposed_modules.contract: For an embedded nonperiodic null bicharacteristic without cusps of a real-principal-symbol operator, construct an infinite-order complex eikonal jet, positive-imaginary transverse Hessian via matrix Riccati, transport hierarchy, Borel realization, O(lambda^-N) residual and Gaussian concentration; state boundary/cutoff conditions.
proposed_modules.source_status: Salo §3.4, pp. 32-39 is explicitly a sketch and refers to Ralston/KKL01/OSSU23 for details. A full module proof or a narrower fully proved local version is still required.

proposed_modules.contract: For real smooth q_j and well-posed forward and terminal-adjoint IBVPs, prove the DN difference pairing equals the integral of (q1-q2)u1 conjugate(u2), with trace regularity explicit.
proposed_modules.source_status: Salo §3.1, pp. 23-24 proves the smooth Green calculation but invokes IBVP well-posedness.

not_proved_or_not_claimed: general Gaussian beam proof in Salo notes
variable-metric well-posedness proof in Salo notes

IP-41_Calderon_conductivity_CGO.existing_supplier_limit: Published Euclidean C1 trace/Green and weak divergence-form Fredholm modules do not supply smooth-manifold DN microlocal theory, the inverse Calderón theorem, or the limiting Carleman estimate.

proposed_modules.contract: For positive smooth gamma and rho=sqrt(gamma), prove v=rho^-1 u transforms div_g(gamma grad_g v)=0 to (-Delta_g+q)u=0 with q=Delta_g rho/rho, and derive Lambda_gamma f=rho_boundary Lambda_q(rho_boundary f)-(partial_nu rho)_boundary f. State trace assumptions and separate recovery of q from recovery of gamma.
proposed_modules.source_status: Salo p. 40 states the interior transform and assigns its algebra to Exercise 4.1; boundary DN conjugacy and its use in conductivity recovery are not developed.

proposed_modules.contract: For real smooth q_j with zero outside each Dirichlet spectrum, define DN maps and prove their difference pairing equals integral (q1-q2)u1 conjugate(u2) using Riemannian Green's identity.
proposed_modules.source_status: Salo §4.2, pp. 49-50 gives a direct proof; nonresonance and manifold Green identity are explicit obligations.

proposed_modules.contract: For positive smooth conductivities on a bounded smooth Euclidean domain with full DN equality, prove equality of all boundary normal derivatives by boundary quasimodes, exact correction, and induction in boundary normal coordinates.
proposed_modules.source_status: Salo §4.1, pp. 42-49 proves the calculation but cites standard energy correction and Hörmander Borel summation foundations. Does not imply interior smooth uniqueness or partial-data uniqueness.

proposed_modules.contract: On compact transversally anisotropic (M,g) within (R x M0, dt^2+g0) with smooth q, prove large-|lambda| solvability of the conjugated operator with L2 remainder bound C/|lambda|, specify domain/boundary hypotheses and duality/Hahn-Banach step, then prove CGO amplitude/remainder product estimates sufficient for the ray-integral limit.
proposed_modules.source_status: Salo §§4.2-4.3, pp. 50-54 outlines CGO and states Proposition 4.11 but proves the crucial Carleman estimate only by reference to DKSU09; full solvability and remainder/product error estimates remain to prove. Theorem 4.1 also requires X-ray injectivity on M0.

proposed_modules.contract: For the cubic semilinear Dirichlet equation, establish small-data well-posedness and sufficient differentiability of the solution/DN map to justify third Fréchet linearization and its four-harmonic-product identity.
proposed_modules.source_status: Salo §4.4, pp. 54-57 calculates the formal identity and sketches concentration; the differentiability theorem is not proved.
